method: rg-based PRODUCED/CONSUMED parity scan at each seam; code-smell sweep across stale comments, unused imports, no-op returns, public re-exports; each candidate triaged via CONNECT/CUT/DECIDE per the skill.

findings.consumer_location: none within inherent.rs or struct_def.rs; actual consumers are tool_registry_impl.rs:17,514,522 and optional_tools.rs:5,535,541
findings.rationale: Both files declare `#![allow(unused_imports)]` at the top, so the dead import ships silently. The same `use` line is duplicated in three other files where the symbols are actually referenced, so the two redundant imports add nothing — only the lint suppression. Removing them would surface a future genuine dead import immediately.
findings.residual_risk: If a future contributor adds a `SessionsListTool` / `SessionsSendTool` reference in inherent.rs or struct_def.rs they will have to add the import again — harmless.

findings.consumer_location: none outside the defining module (only TOOL_CATEGORIES slice consumers iterate &ToolCategory anonymously)
findings.rationale: The struct MUST be `pub` because `pub static TOOL_CATEGORIES: &[ToolCategory]` exposes it in the static's type signature (Rust privacy rules). Not a real severed wire — leave as is.
findings.residual_risk: If the static's element type ever drifts, the type is reachable but unused and could rot; not currently.

findings.consumer_location: none by name outside the defining file; consumers iterate the slice BUILTIN_TOOL_DEFINITIONS anonymously
findings.rationale: Same reachability constraint: the public slice `&[BuiltinToolDefinition]` requires the element type to be public. Keep.
findings.residual_risk: If a tool entry is ever written via a literal that does not match the field order, this type can drift silently. Field order is currently preserved by the in-file tests.

findings.produced_location: src/builtin_tools/meta_tools.rs:5 (doc comment; the field was deleted)
findings.consumer_location: none — `BuiltinToolConfig::tool_catalog` does not exist in src/executor/builtin_registry/config.rs
findings.rationale: The module-doc on `builtin_tools::meta_tools` describes the historical deletion of the meta tools, and references `BuiltinToolConfig.tool_catalog` as the gate that was never set. The field was removed from the config struct but the explanatory doc still names it. Two reasonable moves: (a) rewrite the doc to say "the host wiring that production never completed" so it doesn't dangle on a non-existent field, or (b) leave it as written historical evidence. The intent is clearly historical, not a live reference; the doc is misleading but not load-bearing.
findings.residual_risk: A reader hunting for `BuiltinToolConfig.tool_catalog` will not find it; mild documentation drift only.

findings.rationale: Wired, but with an internal name drift: the field is named for the implementation type (`SessionSetTopicTool`), while the wire name (catalog + dispatch + SHORTHAND_ALIASES `("rename", "session_rename")`) is `session_rename`. The catalog deliberately excludes `session_set_topic` to avoid an alias race (`tool_metadata/aliases.rs::rename_alias_targets_real_session_rename_tool`). Not severed — but a reader grepping for `session_set_topic` finds only the struct field, not the catalog entry. The aliases.rs F1 regression test catches this and is passing.
findings.residual_risk: A new contributor adding the alias `("rename", "session_set_topic")` will fail `rename_alias_targets_real_session_rename_tool` loudly. The drift is documented but easy to miss.

findings.produced: ToolRegistry trait default methods workspace_handle / smart_recall_config_handle / session_context_handle / session_key_handle
findings.consumer_location: src/gateway/execution_engine/execute.rs:699,725,741,744 (all four read and write the shared handle); override at src/executor/builtin_registry/registry/tool_registry_impl.rs:34,43,49,53
findings.rationale: All four trait default methods return `None`. `BuiltinToolRegistry` overrides each one to expose a shared handle, and `ExecutionEngine::execute` writes the per-turn session/workspace/smart-recall profile into them before dispatch. The two-layer design (race-free per-turn `TURN_CONTEXT` task-local preferred, mutable handle as fallback) is explicit in the inline comments at tool_registry_impl.rs:43-44 and execute.rs:709-744. No severed wire.
findings.residual_risk: A new `ToolRegistry` implementor that forgets to override any of the four will silently fall through to `None`, and the dependent tools (memory_search / session-binding) will miss their per-turn scope. Not currently a bug; documented behavior.

findings.rationale: Each extracted submodule defines exactly one `pub(crate) fn build_*` and is invoked exactly once from the parent `with_config` constructor. This is internal structure — `pub(crate)` is intentional. No severed wire.
findings.residual_risk: Submodule growth is bounded by `with_config`'s responsibility; a future added extractor without a call site would be the real warning sign.

findings.produced: ToolRegistry trait — `execute_tool` is the indivisible dispatch match
findings.consumer_location: every ToolRegistry consumer: registry_adapter.rs:372,532,564; gateway/execution_engine/turn_permissions.rs:250; tests/memory_modes_integration.rs (via execute_tool calls); plus dispatchable.rs census every_advertised_builtin_tool_is_dispatchable at lines183-204
findings.rationale: The wire is guarded by `every_advertised_builtin_tool_is_dispatchable` (dispatchable.rs:183): it scans both `BUILTIN_TOOL_DEFINITIONS` and `builder/core_tools.rs::reg(` sites, recovers the dispatch arms from `tool_registry_impl.rs::=>`, and fails the build if any advertised name lacks an arm. Proven to fail by name on `plugin_manage` (see dispatchable.rs:179-180). The fix-on-2026-08-19 for `plugin_manage` is the documented case this guard caught. Mechanically complete.
findings.residual_risk: Future registration shapes (e.g. a new constructor-direct `tools.insert("foo", …)` call outside the two scanned files) would not be picked up. `every_registered_core_tool_is_accounted` (definitions.rs:1989+) and `REG_INSERTED_NAMES` (definitions.rs:1521+) try to keep that honest.

verification: Static only per instructions — cargo check/test intentionally NOT run. All public symbols verified by rg scan across src/, tests/, bin/ (substitute paths: src/bin/aleph-server), interfaces/, crates/, desktop/, bindings/ excluding review-results/, graphify-out/, .worktrees/.
notes: Module is small but very dense —21 files including the 195k-line definitions.rs catalog. The interesting findings are 1) two redundant use-imports allowed by `#![allow(unused_imports)]` in inherent.rs/struct_def.rs, and 2) a stale doc reference in builtin_tools/meta_tools.rs to a deleted BuiltinToolConfig.tool_catalog field. The catalog → dispatch parity is unusually well guarded by a source-level census (dispatchable.rs), which fails the build on a missing arm. The intrinsic name drift between struct field `session_set_topic_tool` and wire name `session_rename` is documented and tested. No severed wires of forms1, 2, 4, or 5 were found; no inert BuiltinToolConfig fields were found. The audit identified8 findings, well under the 10 cap; the `reviewed_no_change` block documents the 7 surfaces I scanned and found intact.
